title: When the Next Step Is Not One Step: Distribution-Aware Execution Modeling for Concurrent Go Programs
abstract: arXiv:2606.17508v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Predicting the next scheduler event of a concurrent program is ill-posed as single-label classification: repeated runs from the same trace prefix produce different, equally valid next events. We formulate next-event prediction for concurrent Go programs as estimating an empirical next-event distribution obtained from repeated executions, and release a benchmark with 945 training examples from hand-written and generated programs and 798 held-out predictions on 54 real-world GoKer bug kernels from systems such as CockroachDB, Kubernetes, gRPC and etcd. We fine-tune Qwen2.5-Coder-7B with low-rank adapters under a cross-entropy objective and a KL-to-empirical-distribution objective and compare them with zero-shot models and trivial baselines. The outcome is a neutral-to-negative result. The fine-tuned adapters (re-evaluated: 36.3% cross-entropy, 33.6% KL; originally reported 36.2% and 35.8%) are statistically indistinguishable from alway

translated_title: 当下一步不止一步：面向并发 Go 程序的分布感知执行建模
translated_abstract: 将并发程序的下一个调度器事件预测视为单标签分类是一个病态问题：从同一轨迹前缀出发的重复运行会产生不同但同样有效的下一事件。我们将并发 Go 程序的下一事件预测形式化为估计从重复执行中获得的经验性下一事件分布，并发布了一个基准，其中包含来自手写与生成程序的 945 个训练样本，以及在来自 CockroachDB、Kubernetes、gRPC 和 etcd 等系统的 54 个真实世界 GoKer 缺陷内核上的 798 个留存预测。我们在交叉熵目标和 KL 散度（对齐经验分布）目标下使用低秩适配器微调 Qwen2.5-Coder-7B，并将其与零样本模型和简单基线进行比较。结果是一个中性偏负面的结果：微调后的适配器（重新评估：交叉熵 36.3%，KL 33.6%；最初报告为 36.2% 和 35.8%）在统计上与总是预测最常见事件的平凡基线难以区分。
tldr: 该论文将并发 Go 程序的“下一事件预测”从单标签分类重新形式化为对经验性下一事件分布的估计，并发布了基于真实 GoKer 缺陷内核的基准，但实验发现使用交叉熵和 KL 目标微调的 Qwen2.5-Coder-7B 适配器与简单基线在统计上无显著差异，是一个中性偏负面的结果。
en_tdlr: This paper reformulates next-event prediction for concurrent Go programs as estimating an empirical next-event distribution rather than single-label classification, releases a benchmark built on real-world GoKer bug kernels, and finds that fine-tuned Qwen2.5-Coder-7B adapters under cross-entropy and KL objectives are statistically indistinguishable from trivial baselines—a neutral-to-negative result.
